races.title: State House, District 88
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mary Belk
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 88 since 2017, after defeating Rob Bryan in 2016. Former insurance adjuster who co-owned a family printing business with her husband and later a vacation rental investment firm. Earned a UNC Charlotte political science degree in 2006.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina listed Belk among its 2026 recommendations, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Mary Belk was born or when, if ever, she moved to North Carolina. Her roots rest on her Charlotte schooling and long local record. The pages we had show no deeds or stated positions on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership limits, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Her campaign site mentions a small-business bill, a class-size delay (HB13) and an opioid-treatment bill, but gives no details or bill numbers for them. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, and no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 90: She attended Garinger High School in Charlotte, was elected to her church council at 19, and has worked in Charlotte business and civic life for about 50 years, but her birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2017 (nine years). Earlier she worked in insurance adjusting, co-owned a family printing business, and co-founded a vacation rental investment partnership. She holds a political science degree.
qual.why: Years of prior legislative service plus business ownership and management put her in the high band. Committee seats and nonprofit or civic board roles were not counted.

cands.name: Ray Craig
cands.bio: Ray Craig was the Republican nominee for North Carolina House District 88 in 2026. He advanced without a primary contest and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Mary Belk. No jobs or offices held could be verified from the sources available.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Ray Craig was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his job history. We found no record of any office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no other statements from him on issues such as data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no endorsements, controversies or foreign ties. The only page available was a short Ballotpedia page that lists his 2026 race.
